title: Inner Incentive is the second-order effort an aligned actor spends overcoming misaligned first-order incentives
content:
A.0.1.1.7 defines Inner Incentive as the second-order incentive a universally aligned actor uses to counteract the first-order (self-interested) incentives that exist pre-Alignment Engineering or that arise from a misaligned structure.

It is the quantity that makes Alignment Artifact Strength meaningful in practice. Inner Incentive is a **cost borne by the aligned actor**: where structure and purpose diverge, someone acting rightly must expend something extra to do so. That makes it a tax levied specifically on good actors, and an unstable foundation — it depends on individual character, does not scale with participation, and is exhausted by repeated demand.

The framework's ambition follows directly: drive required Inner Incentive toward zero by strengthening Artifacts, so that correct behaviour stops depending on anyone's willingness to absorb that cost.
description: It counteracts the self-interested incentives existing pre-Alignment-Engineering or arising from a misaligned structure — making it the hidden tax a weak Artifact imposes on good actors.
